anchors.name: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
anchors.binding: A recommendation adopted by UNESCO's 193 member states
anchors.asks: Human oversight and determination, transparency and explainability, and responsibility and accountability for AI systems across their life cycle.
anchors.evidence: A measured test of the system on your own questions before it leaves pilot, with every failure listed for the official accountable for AI use.

anchors.name: EU AI Act Art 27 and Annex III 5(a)
anchors.binding: EU law; it applies to public bodies that deploy high-risk systems listed in Annex III in the EU
anchors.asks: Before first using a high-risk system listed in Annex III, other than for critical infrastructure, a public body assesses its impact on fundamental rights and notifies the regulator; it can rely on an existing data protection impact assessment. Eligibility for public assistance benefits is an Annex III use.
anchors.evidence: Test results and failure lists that your fundamental rights impact assessment can cite.
